# Generated by the game build. This code/data belongs to the game, not its Gua DLL.
extends Node
const REMOTE_MODE := /*MODE*/
const EXPECTED_SHA256 := /*HASH*/
const PROVIDER_SOURCE := /*SOURCE*/
const PROVIDER_BUILD := /*BUILD*/
const DESCRIPTOR := "res://gua_generated/native/gua.gdextension"
var verified := false

func _enter_tree() -> void:
	if OS.get_name() != "Windows" or not OS.has_feature("x86_64"):
		_refuse("unsupported platform")
		return
	if ProjectSettings.has_setting("dotnet/project/assembly_name") or "C#" in ProjectSettings.get_setting("application/config/features", PackedStringArray()):
		_refuse("unsupported Godot .NET host")
		return
	# For the legitimate Gua extension, class registration happens during DLL load.
	# Reject legacy auto-loading before consulting any Gua API or starting a bridge.
	if ClassDB.class_exists("GuaContext"):
		_refuse("Gua was loaded before game verification; nativeLoaded=true")
		return
	# The GAME verifier contains the expected hash, denies writes/deletes and
	# retains its handles while loading the SDK. A separate GDScript pathname
	# check would leave a check/load race and is intentionally not authoritative.
	if GDExtensionManager.load_extension(DESCRIPTOR) != GDExtensionManager.LOAD_STATUS_OK:
		_refuse("game-owned verifier could not initialize Gua")
		return
	verified = true
	print("Gua game policy verified: ", REMOTE_MODE)

func _refuse(reason: String) -> void:
	push_error("Gua game integrity refused: " + reason)
	if Engine.is_editor_hint():
		return # Never terminate an Editor or lose its unsaved work.
	# SceneTree.quit is deferred and would allow later autoload callbacks to run.
	# On this supported Windows path, terminate immediately instead.
	OS.kill(OS.get_process_id())
